summary: Event streams are authenticated entry points for external events. Types: HMAC shared secret (GitHub), Basic (Datadog, Dynatrace), Token in Authorization or custom header like X-Gitlab-Token (GitLab, ServiceNow), OAuth2 client credentials, OAuth2 with JWT, ECDSA signatures (SendGrid, Twilio), and mTLS with Certificate or Subject subtypes (PagerDuty).
questions: What authentication types do EDA event streams support?
Which event stream type should I use for GitHub webhooks?
Can an event stream use a custom token header like X-Gitlab-Token?
Does Event-Driven Ansible support mTLS event streams?

answer_card.title: Event stream types
answer_card.answer_md:
| Type | How it authenticates | Example vendors |
|---|---|---|
| HMAC | shared secret signature | GitHub |
| Basic | HTTP basic auth | Datadog, Dynatrace |
| Token | token in a header (`Authorization` or custom, e.g. `X-Gitlab-Token`) | GitLab, ServiceNow |
| OAuth2 | client credentials, opaque token | Dynatrace |
| OAuth2 with JWT | client credentials, JWT | Datadog |
| ECDSA | public/private key signature | SendGrid, Twilio |
| mTLS | two-way certs (Certificate or Subject); vendor CA needed at startup | PagerDuty |
